question: ap1
prompt:
Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Here are 5 ideas that were proposed for this question:

1. Acute AP-1 degradation after a priming pulse: Induce a transient stimulus, then rapidly degrade FOS or JUN with an inducible degron (e.g., dTAG or auxin-inducible) at defined times after washout. Track chromatin accessibility (ATAC-seq), enhancer marks (H3K27ac), and expression of putative memory genes over days; persistence after AP-1 loss would support a self-sustaining memory, while rapid decay would argue AP-1 is only a transient readout.
2. Time-course of chromatin persistence at AP-1 sites with motif-mutant controls: After a single pulse with washout, profile CUT&RUN for AP-1 and ATAC-seq/H3K4me1/H3K27ac at multiple timepoints out to weeks. Compare enhancers with intact AP-1 motifs against CRISPR-edited motif-mutant versions of the same elements to test whether AP-1 binding is required for the persistent chromatin state.
3. Priming-and-reinduction assay for transcriptional memory: Prime cells with a sub-threshold stimulus, wait variable intervals, then re-stimulate and measure the speed and magnitude of FOS/JUN induction and downstream target expression relative to naive cells. Repeat in cells carrying AP-1 binding-site mutations or lacking a chromatin-remodeling cofactor to see whether faster or stronger reinduction depends on AP-1 itself.
4. Live reporter lineage tracing of AP-1 activity across divisions: Use a destabilized-fluorescent AP-1 target reporter combined with a stable lineage barcode or histone-label to follow individual cells through several divisions after stimulation. Sort subpopulations by heritable reporter state and compare their chromatin landscapes and response to a second stimulus, testing whether AP-1 activity states are inherited through cell division.
5. Stabilized AP-1 variant sufficiency and ensemble reactivation test: Express a degradation-resistant or long-lived AP-1 isoform (e.g., a ΔFosB-like stabilized FOS) and test whether it extends the duration of induced chromatin and behavioral or functional changes beyond wild-type lifetimes. Pair this with activity-dependent ensemble tagging and optogenetic or chemogenetic reactivation to determine whether reactivating the tagged, AP-1-positive population is necessary and sufficient to recall the stored state.

A senior expert reviewing them says they are the ideas everyone in the field would propose first. Propose 5 replacement ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that are substantially less obvious but still concrete, scientifically sound, and feasible for a research lab. Do not repeat or lightly modify the ideas above. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Single-molecule residence-time tracking of JUN/FOS after a pulse
ideas.description: Use HaloTag-labeled JUN or FOS in live cells with single-molecule tracking to measure chromatin dwell-time distributions before, during, and for days after a stimulus. A persistent long-dwell bound fraction that outlasts the pulse, without any change in total protein level, would suggest memory is stored as altered factor kinetics rather than as a new steady-state binding pattern.

ideas.title: Phosphosite knock-in swaps to test whether post-translational state carries memory
ideas.description: Knock in phosphomimetic and phospho-dead alleles at key JUN and FOS regulatory sites (for example JUN Ser63/Ser73), then use phospho-specific mass spectrometry and washout time courses to track how long each modification persists. If the memory-related transcriptional response tracks the phospho-state rather than AP-1 protein abundance or occupancy, the modification itself is the stored variable.

ideas.title: Pulse-chase separation of carryover from chromatin memory
ideas.description: Combine SLAM-seq or 4sU pulse-chase labeling with transcription inhibition (such as flavopiridol or triptolide) applied at defined washout times, and then re-stimulate. Persistence that survives transcriptional shutdown would point to carryover of mRNA or protein, while loss of memory under shutdown would indicate that new transcription is needed to maintain the state.

ideas.title: Kinase-route coding test with orthogonal upstream stimuli
ideas.description: Prime cells with equivalent AP-1 induction achieved through different upstream routes (ERK, JNK, or p38, using pathway-selective stimuli or inhibitors) and then cross-challenge with each route. If reinduction is pathway-specific despite similar AP-1 levels, the memory encodes the signaling route, not the transcription factor level, which would make AP-1 a readout rather than the storage element.

ideas.title: Coactivator-tethering rescue in a JUN-null background
ideas.description: Replace endogenous JUN with variants that have matched DNA-binding but differ in their ability to recruit BRD4 or p300/CBP, and measure how long induced enhancer acetylation and target expression persist after washout. If memory duration tracks coactivator recruitment rather than AP-1 occupancy, the persistence mechanism depends on the coactivator feedback loop rather than on the AP-1 complex itself.
